question: Which statement best describes Roles, states, and properties?
options: ARIA has three attribute families. A role (role='tablist') tells assistive tech what an element *is*. A state (aria-checked, aria-expanded) describes a condition that changes as the user interacts. A property (aria-label, aria-controls) describes a relatively static characteristic or relationship. Together they fill in semantics the host HTML doesn't natively express.

aria-label supplies an accessible name directly as a string. aria-labelledby points (by id) to visible element(s) that name the control, concatenating their text. aria-describedby points to elements giving extra description (hints, error text) announced after the name. labelledby wins over label; both win over inner text.

1) If a native element/attribute exists, use it instead of ARIA. 2) Don't change native semantics unless you must (don't put role='button' on an <h2>). 3) All interactive ARIA controls must be keyboard usable. 4) Don't put role='presentation' or aria-hidden='true' on a focusable element — you'll hide it from screen readers while it's still tabbable. 5) Every interactive element needs an accessible name.

aria-hidden='true' removes an element and its subtree from the accessibility tree while leaving it visible on screen — useful for decorative icons or duplicated text. Never apply it to focusable content: a sighted keyboard user could still tab to an element that screen readers can't see, creating a 'phantom focus' bug.

question: Which statement best describes Naming: aria-label, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby?
options: aria-label supplies an accessible name directly as a string. aria-labelledby points (by id) to visible element(s) that name the control, concatenating their text. aria-describedby points to elements giving extra description (hints, error text) announced after the name. labelledby wins over label; both win over inner text.

aria-expanded='true|false' on a toggle (disclosure, menu, accordion) tells assistive tech whether the controlled region is open. aria-controls points (by id) to the element it shows/hides. Together they let a screen-reader user understand a button collapses/expands a specific panel.

ARIA is essential for custom widgets HTML can't model (tabs, comboboxes, tree views, complex grids) and for live announcements. It's harmful when it overrides correct native semantics, lacks the required keyboard behavior, points to missing ids, or hides focusable content. The data shows pages with ARIA often have *more* errors — 'No ARIA is better than bad ARIA.'
